subject: biology
title: Sex determination
key_idea: Females have two X chromosomes (XX). Males have an X and a Y (XY). Every egg carries an X, and a sperm carries X or Y. So the sperm that fertilises the egg decides the sex, and the chance of a boy or a girl is 50% each time.

blocks.text: One pair of chromosomes decides whether a person is male or female. This section covers which chromosomes each sex has.

items.meaning: The pair of chromosomes that carries the genes that determine sex. They are called X and Y.
A picture of the chromosomes found in the nucleus of a single cell.

items: Ordinary human body cells contain 23 pairs of chromosomes.
22 pairs control characteristics only.
One pair carries the genes that determine sex.
In **females** the sex chromosomes are the same: **XX**.
In **males** the sex chromosomes are different: **XY**.
Whether a person has a Y chromosome or not decides their sex.
Females are XX and males are XY.
The Y chromosome makes a person male.
22 pairs of chromosomes control characteristics only.

blocks.text: Gametes have half the chromosomes, so each gamete has one sex chromosome. Choose the parents below to see the cross.

diagram.alt: A Punnett square for sex determination. The mother is XX and the father is XY. The offspring are two XX females and two XY males.

items.text: The mother is XX. The father is XY.
Every egg has an X. Half of the sperm have an X and half have a Y.
The offspring are XX, XX, XY and XY.
Two boxes in four are XY. The probability of a boy is 0.5 (50%, ½, 1 in 2) and so is the probability of a girl.

items: The sex is decided at fertilisation by the sperm: an X sperm gives a girl and a Y sperm gives a boy.
Which sperm fertilises the egg is random, so every pregnancy has a 50% chance of a boy and a 50% chance of a girl.
So a family can have four children of one sex, or three of one sex and one of the other, instead of two and two.
If all sperm with an X chromosome were destroyed, every child would be XY, so only males would be born.
Every egg has an X. A sperm has X or Y.
The probability of a boy or a girl is 0.5 each, not a ratio of 50 : 50.
Which sperm fertilises the egg is a chance event.

blocks.text: Exam questions give data on the numbers of males and females. You may need to share a total using a ratio.

items: At birth in England and Wales there are 105 males for every 100 females.
Over the whole population there are 98 males for every 100 females.
More males are born, but fewer males are alive in the whole population. This is because males do not live as long, on average.

checks.q: Give the sex chromosomes of a human male and of a human female.
Describe how sex is determined in humans.
checks.a: Eggs (female gametes) contain an X chromosome. Sperm (male gametes) contain either an X or a Y. XX is female and XY is male, so the sperm that fertilises the egg decides the sex.

checks.q: A couple already have three daughters. What is the probability that their fourth child is a boy? Explain.
checks.a: 0.5 (50%). Each pregnancy is a separate chance: it depends on whether an X or a Y sperm fertilises the egg.

worked_example.question:
Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes in each body cell.

One pair of chromosomes determines sex.

In some families all children are the same sex.

Give the reason why.
answer_points: It is a 50% chance whether the sperm cell that fertilised the egg has an X or a Y chromosome.
Each child (pregnancy) has a 50% chance of being male or female, so all can be the same sex.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the idea that the sex of each child is a separate chance.

worked_example.question:
A karyogram is a picture of the chromosomes found in the nucleus of a single cell.

State the probability that a child will be male.
worked_example.tip: 50 : 50 is a ratio, not a probability, and scores 0.

worked_example.question:
Describe how sex is determined in humans.

You may use a genetic diagram in your answer.
answer_points: Sperm (male gametes) contain either an X or a Y chromosome, and eggs (female gametes) contain an X chromosome.
XX is female and XY is male.
worked_example.tip: A correct Punnett square that shows XY is male and XX is female earns both marks. Without the labels it earns the gamete mark only.
